article.headline: Pelosi Exercises Her Options, and the Internet Takes Notes
article.lede: Nancy Pelosi's latest Periodic Transaction Report landed, revealing that the former House Speaker exercised deep in-the-money calls on Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, and Tempus AI — netting 20,000 shares — while unloading sizable stakes in Apple, Disney, and PayPal.
article.body:
The disclosure itself is unremarkable as paperwork goes: a two-page filing submitted to the House Clerk's office, as required by the *STOCK Act*, the 2012 law that compels members of Congress and their spouses to report securities transactions above $1,000 within 45 days. What makes Pelosi's version of the form appointment reading is that it consistently describes positions that, viewed in hindsight, look less like portfolio management and more like a guided tour of the market's winners.

The mechanics here are worth pausing on. Each of the four bought positions came via exercising a *deep in-the-money call option* — a contract whose strike price sits well below the stock's current market price, meaning almost all of its value is "intrinsic" rather than speculative. A deep ITM call behaves almost identically to owning the underlying shares outright (in the jargon, its *delta* — the ratio of option-price move to stock-price move — approaches 1.0), while tying up less capital than an outright purchase. Paul Pelosi reportedly bought the calls in January 2025 at strikes of $150 for Alphabet and Amazon, $80 for Nvidia, and $20 for Tempus AI, then exercised them roughly a year later. Over that period, Tempus AI gained 121 percent, Alphabet 75 percent, and Nvidia 41 percent. The combined weighted return was approximately 41.7 percent — roughly double the S&P 500 over the same stretch.

Tempus AI deserves a brief introduction for readers who do not monitor the healthcare-AI space. Founded by Eric Lefkofsky of Groupon fame, Tempus applies machine learning to clinical data — genomic sequencing, radiology images, oncology records — to help physicians choose therapies and to sell de-identified data and algorithms to pharmaceutical companies. It went public in June 2024 and, in its fiscal 2025, reported revenue of $1.27 billion, up 83 percent year-on-year. Whether that warrants the Pelosi family's entry into the stock at a $20 strike is a question the filing does not answer.

The ritual of tracking these disclosures has itself become an industry. Quiver Quantitative aggregates congressional transaction reports and publishes copy-trading signals; Unusual Whales, a financial-data firm with an eye for spectacle, launched an ETF — ticker NANC, a not-subtle nod — that mechanically replicates Democratic members' disclosed trades. The fund holds $258 million in assets and has returned 74 percent since its February 2023 launch, outpacing its Republican-tracking counterpart, GOP. The rub, as Unusual Whales cheerfully admits, is that the mandated 30-to-45-day reporting lag means the fund buys after the disclosure, not with it — a structural disadvantage that probably explains why NANC has not fully replicated Pelosi's decade-long cumulative return of 816 percent.

Whether that outperformance reflects prescience, luck, a technology-heavy portfolio that happened to ride the AI boom, or something less flattering is the question that has resisted clean resolution for years. Defenders note that a concentrated bet on mega-cap technology names was simply a good idea throughout the 2020s, and that survivorship bias inflates the legend: the trades that aged poorly attract less Twitter engagement than the ones that did not. Critics note that the same members who sit on committees overseeing telecommunications, defence procurement, and financial regulation are the ones reporting the most active portfolios — a coincidence that 86 percent of Americans, according to recent polling, would prefer to eliminate by banning congressional stock ownership outright. The 119th Congress has seen more than two dozen bills introduced to that end, including a Senate measure, S.1879, that would prohibit members, spouses, and dependent children from owning individual securities entirely. None has yet passed.

concepts.definition: The Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act (2012) prohibits members of Congress, their staff, and certain executive-branch officials from trading on material non-public information obtained through their official duties. It also requires them to publicly disclose securities transactions above $1,000 within 45 days via Periodic Transaction Reports filed with the House Clerk or Senate Secretary.

A call option whose strike price is substantially below the current market price of the underlying stock. Because most of the option's value is intrinsic (the gap between strike and market price) rather than speculative, it behaves almost identically to owning the shares outright — its delta approaches 1.0 — while requiring less upfront capital than a direct stock purchase.

The standardised disclosure form that members of Congress and covered federal employees must file within 45 days of any securities transaction exceeding $1,000 in value. PTRs are publicly posted by the House Clerk and Senate Secretary and form the raw data for congressional trading trackers.

An options metric expressing how much the option's price moves for every $1 move in the underlying stock. A delta of 1.0 means the option tracks the stock dollar-for-dollar; deep in-the-money calls typically have deltas between 0.85 and 1.0.

article.fact_check: The disclosed transactions — 5,000 shares each of GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, and TEM acquired via exercising calls, plus sales of AAPL, DIS, and PYPL — are consistent with the Periodic Transaction Report filed January 23, 2026 as reported by the Motley Fool and Quiver Quantitative. Strike prices ($150 GOOGL/AMZN, $80 NVDA, $20 TEM) and purchase date (January 14, 2025) are sourced from public PTR data. The 41.7% weighted portfolio return figure comes from Motley Fool analysis of the period between purchase and exercise dates. Pelosi decade-long cumulative return of 816% is cited by Quiver Quantitative. The NANC ETF AUM of $258 million and 74% return since February 2023 inception are sourced from Unusual Whales and Barchart. The 86% public support figure for a trading ban is from Campaign Legal Center citing polling data. 13,000 congressional trades totalling $635.5 million in 2025 is from Harvard Journal on Legislation citing Quiver Quantitative data. Tempus AI FY2025 revenue of $1.27 billion (+83% YoY) is from public filings. The AAPL (45,000 shares), DIS (10,000), and PYPL (5,000) sale figures are taken directly from the tweet text as the PTR filing itself was not independently verified beyond secondary reporting.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_amzn.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
ticker_amzn.blurb: Amazon operates the world's largest e-commerce marketplace and the leading cloud infrastructure platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS generates the majority of Amazon's operating profit despite representing a minority of total revenue. The company also has significant positions in digital advertising, streaming (Prime Video), and logistics infrastructure. Amazon is a major investor in AI, both through AWS cloud AI services and through a multi-billion-dollar strategic stake in Anthropic.
ticker_amzn.recent: Amazon reported FY2025 revenue exceeding $650 billion, with AWS growing at roughly 17% annually and crossing $100 billion in run-rate revenue. The advertising segment has become a meaningful profit contributor. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026), with the stock gaining approximately 10% over that period — the weakest performer in the Pelosi 2026 exercise batch.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

sources.title: Nvidia Stock Analysis 2026: AI Demand — Intellectia
NVIDIA Stock Forecast: AI Chip Demand — TIKR

ticker_tem.name: Tempus AI, Inc.
ticker_tem.blurb: Tempus AI applies machine learning to clinical and genomic data to advance precision medicine — the practice of tailoring medical treatment to individual patients based on their genetic and molecular profiles. The company operates in oncology, cardiology, radiology, and neuropsychiatry, offering genomic sequencing diagnostics, AI-powered clinical decision tools, and a proprietary data platform that it licenses to pharmaceutical companies for drug discovery. Founded in 2015 by Eric Lefkofsky (co-founder of Groupon), Tempus went public in June 2024.
ticker_tem.recent: Tempus reported FY2025 revenue of $1.27 billion, an 83% increase year-on-year, driven by its data and genomics segments. The company narrowed losses to -$245 million. Management guided for 25% revenue growth in 2026 and positive adjusted EBITDA of $65 million. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $20 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026), with TEM shares returning approximately 121% over that period — the strongest performer in the disclosure batch.

Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker

ticker_dis.name: The Walt Disney Company
ticker_dis.blurb: Disney is a global media and entertainment conglomerate whose assets span theme parks, film studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm), the ABC broadcast network, ESPN, and the Disney+ and Hulu streaming platforms. The company has undergone significant restructuring under returning CEO Bob Iger, who returned in 2022 to stabilise the company after a turbulent period under his successor. Disney's streaming transition has been costly but Disney+ reached profitability in late 2024.
ticker_dis.recent: Disney reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $93 billion. The experiences segment (theme parks and cruises) remains the primary profit engine. The company is pursuing ESPN's transition to a direct-to-consumer streaming service and has made moves to consolidate streaming assets. Paul Pelosi sold 10,000 shares of DIS per the January 2026 PTR disclosure.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker

ticker_pypl.name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
ticker_pypl.blurb: PayPal operates one of the world's largest digital payments networks, facilitating transactions between consumers and merchants via its PayPal wallet, Venmo peer-to-peer app, Braintree payment gateway, and Honey shopping tool. Spun off from eBay in 2015, PayPal was for years one of the fastest-growing fintech companies globally; it has since faced intensified competition from Apple Pay, Google Pay, Stripe, and bank-issued digital wallets, compressing both growth and margins.
ticker_pypl.recent: PayPal has been undergoing a strategic overhaul under CEO Alex Chriss, who took the helm in 2023, focusing on profitable growth over transaction volume. The company has invested in AI-driven checkout personalisation and advertising capabilities. Despite a recovery in the stock price from multi-year lows, PayPal trades at a significant discount to its 2021 peak. Paul Pelosi sold 5,000 shares of PYPL per the January 2026 PTR disclosure.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker

ticker_nanc.name: Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF
ticker_nanc.blurb: NANC is an exchange-traded fund launched in February 2023 by Unusual Whales (a financial-data firm known for tracking options flow and congressional trading activity) in partnership with Subversive Capital. The fund replicates the disclosed stock trades of Democratic members of Congress and their spouses, weighted and rebalanced according to publicly filed Periodic Transaction Reports. Its ticker is an explicit reference to Nancy Pelosi, whose trading disclosures have attracted outsized public attention. A companion fund, GOP, tracks Republican members' trades.
ticker_nanc.recent: As of early 2026, NANC holds approximately $258 million in assets under management and has returned roughly 74% since its February 2023 inception, outpacing both the S&P 500 and its GOP counterpart over the same period. The fund's portfolio is heavily weighted toward mega-cap technology names — Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet feature prominently — reflecting the actual disclosed trades of Democratic members. A structural lag exists: the mandatory 30-to-45-day reporting window means the fund buys disclosed positions after the fact, preventing it from fully replicating the returns of the members it tracks. Expense ratio: 0.75%.

poster_amitisinvesting.blurb: Amit Kukreja is a New York-based financial content creator and entrepreneur who publishes under the handle @amitisinvesting across X, YouTube (approximately 117,000 subscribers), and Substack. A Rutgers Business School graduate, he transitioned from finance to digital media around 2021, building a following focused on growth-stock analysis — particularly technology companies and AI plays such as Palantir. He hosts the Basis Points podcast, has made angel investments in private companies, and previously founded Audea, an AI-powered search engine for spoken-word audio. His congressional-trading posts, which parse freshly filed Periodic Transaction Reports, are among his most widely shared content.
poster_amitisinvesting.credibility_note: Kukreja presents himself as a financial educator and market commentator rather than a licensed investment adviser. His congressional-trading posts aggregate public disclosure data rather than offering original analytical claims; the underlying PTR filings are verifiable through the House Clerk's public database. His technology-sector commentary reflects a bullish growth-stock orientation.
